key_insight: A polymorphic high-entropy oxide photocatalyst paired with microalgae as a sacrificial agent substantially boosts solar-driven CO2 reduction to CO and CH4.
engineering_relevance: The study suggests a sustainable reactor strategy that couples biological CO2 scavenging with engineered photocatalysts to improve carbon conversion efficiency.
method: Designed an AB2O6-type high-entropy oxide, (Cs1/7Ba4/7Bi2/7)(Nb1/2Ta1/2)2O6, with layered perovskite/pyrochlore polymorphy.
Used Cs and Ba to raise surface basicity, Bi to promote polarization/charge separation, and Nb/Ta frameworks to support charge transport.
Compared photocatalytic CO2 conversion with no sacrificial agent, with microplastics, and with microalgae.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that adding microalgae increases CO and CH4 production by about 10-fold and 4-fold, respectively, versus the HEO-only system.
watch_item: The approach depends on integrating and managing living microalgae in the photocatalytic workflow, which may complicate reactor stability, separation, and long-term operation.
paper_title: Sustainable photocatalytic CO2 conversion using microalgae as a carbon-negative scavenger
